items.title: 10.9 Amount of substance produced during electrolysis

source_refs.note: Topic 10.9 with Sample Problem 10.5, printed page 222.

blocks.text: The value of F can be used to calculate the mass of substance deposited at an electrode and the volume of gas produced at an electrode.

blocks.title: Sample Problems 10.5
blocks.problem: Calculate the mass of lead (Pb) deposited at the cathode during electrolysis when a current of 1.50 A flows through molten lead(II) bromide (PbBr₂) for 20.0 min. (relative atomic mass, Ar value: [Pb] = 207; F = 96500 C mol⁻¹)
steps:
Step 1 Write the half-equation for the reaction.
Pb²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Pb(s)

Step 2 Find the number of coulombs required to deposit 1 mole of product at the electrode.
2 moles of electrons are required per mole of Pb formed = 2F = 2 × 96500 = 193000 C mol⁻¹

Step 3 Calculate the charge transferred during the electrolysis.
Q = I × t = 1.50 × 20 × 60 = 1800 C

Step 4 Calculate the mass by simple proportion using the relative atomic mass.
193000 C deposits 1 mole Pb, which is 207 g Pb
